note: This is a sample conversation, so you can see how it feels. It isn't a real customer.
title: Example: a mobile bike tune-up stand

messages.author: person
messages.body: I fix bikes out of a cargo trailer at the Saturday market and want to do weekday house calls too. Right now people just text me. I'd like a simple site that shows what I do, my prices, and lets people ask for a tune-up without a long back-and-forth.

messages.author: bot
messages.label: Saji Tori
messages.body:
Thanks, this is a clear start. A few questions so the plan fits you:

1. Who books most: commuters, families, or weekend riders?
2. Which neighborhoods will you drive to?
3. Do you want people to pick a time, or send a request you confirm?

messages.author: person
messages.body: Mostly commuters and a few families. North and East side only. I'd rather confirm each request myself.

messages.author: bot
messages.label: Saji Tori
messages.body:
Here's a simple plan to start from.

What you offer: three tune-up levels with set prices, plus house calls in two areas.
Who it's for: commuters who need their bike back fast, and families with several bikes.
What the site needs: one page with your services and prices, the market hours, a map of the two house-call areas, a short request form (name, bike, area, a few times that work), and a few photos.
What can wait: online payment and a full booking calendar.

I'm bringing in Wren, our website designer, to write a starter script for your website.

messages.author: status
messages.body: Wren says your script should take about 3–5 minutes. You can close this page and come back.

messages.author: bot
messages.label: Wren
messages.body:
Two quick questions before I write it:
1. Any colors you like, or should I pick something calm and outdoorsy?
2. What should the request button say?

messages.author: status
messages.body: Your script is getting a quick look-over.

messages.author: bot
messages.label: Wren
messages.body:
Build a one-page placeholder website for a mobile bike tune-up business (business name: [Your Business Name]).

Style: friendly and outdoorsy. Colors: forest green with orange buttons. Large readable text. Works well on phones.

Sections, in order:
1. Header: business name, one line "Bike tune-ups at the market and at your door", and an orange button "Request a tune-up" that scrolls to the form.
2. Services and prices: three cards (Basic, Standard, Full) with placeholder prices and a one-line description each.
3. Where to find us: Saturday market hours (placeholder) and a simple map area showing two house-call zones labeled North and East.
4. Photos: a gallery of 6 placeholder images.
5. Request form: name, phone or email, bike type, area (North / East), and three preferred times. A note under the button: "We'll confirm by text."
6. Footer: contact placeholder and "© [Year] [Your Business Name]".

Use placeholder text in brackets wherever a real detail is needed.
